title: Open direct images with arbitrary finite allowable coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by
an integer invertible in $k$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$
be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes. For every
$K\in D^b_c(X,A)$, one has $Rj_*K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$.
The notation refers to bounded constructible complexes, and ordinary derived categories.

proof.text: Choose a positive integer $N$ with $NA=0$ and $N$ invertible in $k$. First consider a constructible $A$-sheaf $F$. If $N=1$, then $A=0$ and $F=0$, and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise write $N=\prod_{\ell\mid N}\ell^{e_\ell}$. Choose integers $c_\ell$ congruent to $1$ modulo $\ell^{e_\ell}$ and to $0$ modulo all other prime powers. On every $N$-torsion module their sum acts as $1$, their pairwise products as $0$, and each $c_\ell$ acts idempotently. Thus $F=\bigoplus_{\ell\mid N}F_\ell$, where $F_\ell=\operatorname{im}(c_\ell:F\to F)$ is killed by $\ell^{e_\ell}$. Images are kernels of cokernels, so the constructible Serre theorem makes these $A$-sheaves constructible. Filter each by $F_\ell\supset\ell F_\ell\supset\cdots\supset\ell^{e_\ell}F_\ell=0$. Applying the same kernel/cokernel assertion to multiplication by $\ell^r$ and to the inclusions shows that all filtration terms and quotients $Q_{\ell,r}=\ell^rF_\ell/\ell^{r+1}F_\ell$ are constructible $A$-sheaves. Each quotient is killed by $\ell$.

On each stratum trivializing a quotient $Q=Q_{\ell,r}$ as a finite $A$-module sheaf, its underlying finite additive group $M$ is killed by $\ell$ and hence is canonically an $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector space. The same trivializations are $\mathbf F_\ell$-linear, since multiplication by a residue class is repeated addition. Thus $Q$, with these canonical scalars, is a constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf with the same underlying abelian sheaf. The prime $\ell$ divides $N$, so $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$. The prime-field open-image corollary gives a finite range of nonzero cohomology for $Rj_{*,\mathbf F_\ell}Q$, all constructible over $\mathbf F_\ell$. The general module/abelian comparison, applied separately with coefficients $A$ and $\mathbf F_\ell$, identifies the underlying abelian sheaves of $R^qj_{*,A}Q$ and $R^qj_{*,\mathbf F_\ell}Q$ for every $q$. It does not require $A$ itself to be an $\mathbf F_\ell$-algebra.

The coefficient comparison in Step 2 is through an exact forgetful functor, so zero underlying abelian cohomology implies zero $A$-module cohomology (faithfulness detects a zero identity). Its nonzero underlying abelian sheaves are finite locally constant on a finite stratification. Here is explicitly why their inherited $A$-action makes them constructible $A$-sheaves on the same strata. On a stratum, choose an etale neighborhood of a geometric point trivializing the additive sheaf as a finite group $M$. For each of the finitely many pairs $(a,m)\in A\times M$, the section $a m$ has a germ equal to a unique element of $M$ at that point. Refine the neighborhood so that this equality of sections holds, and take the common refinement for all pairs. All action tables are then constant and satisfy the module laws, since the original action does. The additive trivialization is consequently an isomorphism with the constant sheaf of this finite $A$-module. Such neighborhoods cover the stratum. Hence every $R^qj_{*,A}Q$ is constructible, and the finite cohomological range from Step 2 is unchanged.

The module direct-image functor $j_*$ is additive and left exact, and the source module-sheaf category has enough injectives. Apply the derived-functor long exact sequence to $0\to\ell^{r+1}F_\ell\to\ell^rF_\ell\to Q_{\ell,r}\to0$. More generally, if $Rj_*U$ and $Rj_*W$ are bounded constructible and $0\to U\to V\to W\to0$ is exact, its long exact sequence writes $R^qj_*V$ as an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(R^{q-1}j_*W\to R^qj_*U)$ by $\ker(R^qj_*W\to R^{q+1}j_*U)$. The constructible Serre theorem applies to these kernels, cokernels and extensions. Outside the union of the two outer cohomological ranges, both adjacent outer terms $R^qj_*U,R^qj_*W$ vanish, so exactness gives $R^qj_*V=0$. Starting from $\ell^{e_\ell}F_\ell=0$ and descending in $r$, Steps 2-3 prove the assertion for $F_\ell$. Assemble the finitely many $F_\ell$ using the split short exact sequences for partial direct sums and the same argument. This proves $Rj_*F\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ for every constructible $A$-sheaf $F$.

proof.text: Now choose $a\le b$ with $\mathcal H^qK=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. The module-sheaf categories on $X$ and $Y$ are Grothendieck abelian; $j_*$ is left exact additive as above. A bounded below injective representative of $K$ exists, so the bounded-below-complex hypothesis of the truncation spectral-sequence theorem is satisfied. Applying that theorem gives $E_2^{p,q}=R^pj_*\mathcal H^qK\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rj_*K)$, with $p\ge0$, eventual stabilization at every bidegree, and a finite exhaustive separated filtration of each abutment with associated graded $E_\infty^{p,q}$. Step 4 applies to each of the finitely many constructible sheaves $\mathcal H^qK$; choose a common nonnegative integer $B$ bounding the positive degrees of all their direct images. Thus the $E_2$ page is constructible and supported in the rectangle $0\le p\le B$, $a\le q\le b$.

Every successive page is the kernel of its outgoing differential modulo the image of its incoming differential; images are kernels of cokernels. Repeated use of the constructible Serre theorem therefore makes each stabilized $E_\infty^{p,q}$ constructible. No new nonzero bidegree appears after $E_2$. For each total degree $n$, the finite filtration supplied by the truncation theorem and its graded-piece identifications reconstruct $\mathcal H^n(Rj_*K)$ by finitely many extensions of these constructible graded pieces. It is constructible. If $n<a$ or $n>b+B$, every graded piece is zero, and finite exhaustive separated filtration implies $\mathcal H^n(Rj_*K)=0$. Hence $Rj_*K$ is bounded constructible in the ordinary etale derived category with its original $A$-coefficients.
